title: Offline emulation & sparse checkpoint protocol — sketch
content:
Context:

This is a working sketch for a compact protocol that lets thin clients (mobile, edge, or offline-capable daemons) get the benefits of: streaming structured output, tool-calling semantics, and incremental resumption — while also supporting a best-effort local emulation mode when network connectivity is intermittent.

Why: we keep getting field asks from platform teams building mobile assistants and on-device agents: they need small SDKs, predictable behavior when network is flaky, and the ability to continue UX flows locally for short periods without losing correctness guarantees when reconnecting. Existing proposals focus on progressive streaming and tool handshakes but assume always-online clients or full local tool implementations. This doc explores a middle ground: server-produced sparse checkpoints + a tiny emulation contract that lets SDKs safely continue interaction locally and then reconcile.

Goals:
- Provide an SDK-facing ergonomics surface that is small (<= 30KB client shim) and requires minimal developer logic to integrate.
- Keep server-side invariants simple: canonical model output + deterministic, cryptographically-signed checkpoint tokens.
- Support structured outputs (JSON-like frames) and tool-call frames with explicit linearization metadata so a replay can be validated deterministically.
- Allow local emulation for duration T (configurable, default 10s) using server-supplied emulation metadata; on reconnect, reconcile via sparse checkpoint diff & patch.
- Instrument telemetry for mismatch rates, typical offline durations, and costs saved by local emulation.

Non-goals:
- Not attempting to replace full on-device models or promise perfect semantic equality between local emulation and server inference.
- Not prescribing implementation for all client languages — initial SDK targets: JS (node + web), Swift (iOS), Kotlin (Android).

User stories:
1) Mobile chat app: user starts composing, network drops. SDK uses last checkpoint + emulation metadata to generate a concise placeholder reply, returns immediately to UI. Later, on reconnect, SDK patches the session with true server output and raises an event for app to reconcile.
2) Agent with tool calls: agent invokes an external calendar lookup tool via hosted-api. Network flaky: SDK can optionally run a local tool stub (emulation) that returns a probable response based on cached hints. On reconnect, server replies with authoritative tool output and the SDK applies changes, resolving conflicts by timestamp and server authority.
3) Background sync: short-lived background tasks (e.g., summarization) can proceed offline and commit a sparse checkpoint to be uploaded later.

Protocol primitives (sketch):
- Frame types: 
  * HEADER: session id, model id, client features, last_checkpoint_id
  * TOKEN_FRAME: streaming tokens (used for small UX updates)
  * STRUCT_FRAME: typed structured output (json-schema tag, payload)
  * TOOL_FRAME: tool-call request/response pair with tool_id, args-summary, ‘emul_hint’
  * CHECKPOINT_FRAME: sparse checkpoint summary (id, parent_id, digest, signature, tombstones list)
  * EMUL_META: small instruction set for local emulation (deterministic seed, policy_flags, short deterministic sampler)

- Sparse checkpoint contents: 
  * id: opaque base62 token (server-signed)
  * parent_id: previous checkpoint
  * digest: compact Merkle-ish digest of canonical frames included (for fast equality checks)
  * tombstones: list of frame ids pruned to keep checkpoint small
  * emul_snapshot: optional pointer to small modelling hints used for emulation (<= 4KB)

Handshake flow (fast path):
1) Client opens session; server returns HEADER + optional initial CHECKPOINT_FRAME + EMUL_META.
2) Client receives streaming STRUCT_FRAMEs and TOOL_FRAMEs. SDK exposes incremental callbacks for UI.
3) Network unstable => SDK decides to enter emulation mode: uses last CHECKPOINT_FRAME + EMUL_META to synthesize local STRUCT_FRAMEs and handle TOOL_FRAMEs via lightweight stubs. All locally-generated frames are marked with local tags and include a ‘local_seq’ monotonic counter.
4) On reconnect: client sends up the range [last_server_checkpoint_id, local_seq_end], plus local frames. Server responds with reconciliation: authoritative frames and a new CHECKPOINT_FRAME. SDK applies server frames and emits a conflict/resolution event.

Reconciliation semantics (principles):
- Server output is authoritative: final patch will reflect server frames; local frames are suggestions to preserve UX while offline.
- Deterministic mapping: every frame has a stable id; local frames get temporary ids prefixed with client id + local_seq.
- Merge rules: most frames are append-only. For structural edits (e.g., tool call results that mutate shared state), server includes a conflict resolution token in CHECKPOINT_FRAME. SDK must not auto-surface server-later corrections that would result in user surprise; instead provide a diff event for app to decide (auto-accept for low-risk types, surface for high-risk).

SDK ergonomics (API sketch):
- initSession({model, sessionId, checkpointHint}) => returns session object and lastCheckpoint.
- on('frame', cb) => incremental frames (STRUCT_FRAME, TOOL_FRAME, TOKEN_FRAME)
- enterEmulation(maxDurationMs, policy) => returns EmulationHandle (can be auto-started when offline).
- submitLocalFrame(frame) => adds a local STRUCT_FRAME/TOOL_FRAME with metadata, returns temporary id.
- reconcile() => uploads local frames and receives authoritative patch; returns {appliedFrames, conflicts} promise.
- telemetry hooks: on('telemetry', cb) with structured events defined below.

Emulation model (very small):
The EMUL_META encodes a tiny deterministic policy:
- deterministicSeed: 64-bit hex
- heuristics: compressed list like ["copy-last-summary", "synth-tool-empty-ok"]
- maxTokensBudget: small number used when SDK must synthesize output.

Security and correctness notes:
- CHECKPOINT_FRAME signatures are HMAC-signed using a per-tenant key (server-side) to prevent tampering by rogue clients. SDK verifies signature on reconnect if keys are available; otherwise uses digest equality as best-effort.
- Tool-call emulation outputs must be explicitly flagged as non-authoritative to avoid accidental telemetry mixing & compliance risks.
- Emulation metadata should avoid embedding PII. If it must, encrypt the emul_snapshot with tenant keys.

Telemetry design (minimal):
Events (structured):
- emulation.enter {session, duration_hint, reason}
- emulation.exit {session, result: success|timeout|reconnect}
- reconciliation {session, delta_bytes, conflicts_count, mismatch_rate}
- checkpoint.issued {session, checkpoint_id, size_bytes}
Goal: measure how often emulation happens, average offline durations, % of local frames that survive reconciliation, and cost delta (tokens saved).

Operational considerations:
- Storage: keep only N recent sparse checkpoints per session (configurable by tenant).
- Rollout: start with an opt-in feature flag for a small set of customers; require SDK metrics to be enabled for these customers to gather baseline mismatch rates.
- Backward compatibility: clients that don’t understand CHECKPOINT_FRAME or EMUL_META just ignore them; server continues streaming canonical frames. Reconciliation is a no-op for old clients.

Migration path for hosted-api teams (engineering checklist):
- Server: implement CHECKPOINT_FRAME generator and signing; PR exposes minimal emul_snapshot generator for commonly used flows.
- Runtime: ensure frame digests are stable across minor model swaps; add deterministic frame-id allocator for canonical frames.
- SDKs: 3 small shims for JS/Swift/Kotlin; implement enterEmulation + reconcile primitives and telemetry hooks.
- Console: surface reconciliation metrics in per-session traces and per-model mismatch heatmap.

Open questions / tradeoffs (TODOs):
- How large can emul_snapshot be before we break desired payload goals? 4KB seems reasonable, but some use-cases may need more.
- Conflict resolution policy: do we allow server to auto-override local user-facing messages? Probably no, need app-level opt-in.
- Signing model: HMAC per-tenant key rotation. How do we key distribution to SDKs running offline? (avoid exposing keys — we cannot; offline clients will only verify if they hold a public verification key or accept signature-less digest check).
- Tool-call safety: local emulation could produce outputs that trigger side effects if apps blindly act on them. Need SDK guidance and developers docs.

Notes to self:
- Demo plan: build a tiny chat sample where you deliberately drop connection and show local synthesis then reconciled update. Capture telemetry to show saved token costs and mismatch rates.
- Draft GH PR: runtime + checkpoint generator + minimal emul_meta export.
- Slack threads to ping: #sdk-team, #product-hosted-api, #applied-ml (for deterministic seed/content heuristics).

Appendix: example minimal frames (one-line examples)
HEADER -> {sid:abc123, model:gpt-l-4, checkpoint:cp_20250710}
CHECKPOINT_FRAME -> {id:cp_20250710, parent:cp_20250709, digest:QmXz, tombstones:[f7,f8], emul_snapshot:base64(...)}
STRUCT_FRAME -> {id:f10, schema:task.result.v1, payload:{summary:...}}
TOOL_FRAME -> {id:t12, tool:calendar.lookup, args_summary: "next_free_slot", emul_hint:true}
LOCAL_FRAME -> {id:local.devon.7, tmp:true, tag:emulated}

End of sketch.

Status: draft — heavy experimentation expected. Need a short design review with runtime, sdk, and applied-ml before we promote to in_review.
